title: Quiz: Diagnosing and Handling Missing Values

questions.text: A patient's BMI is missing because they never visited a GP and no measurement was taken. Which missing data mechanism does this represent?
questions.explanation: MAR: the missingness depends on an observed variable (GP visit frequency). The BMI value itself is not what causes the missingness — it is the behaviour (attending GP) that determines whether BMI gets recorded.

questions.text: Why should a binary missingness indicator be added when imputing a numeric variable?
options: It replaces the need for imputation
It allows downstream models to learn from the pattern of missingness itself
It prevents the imputed column from being used in the model
It converts the variable from numeric to categorical
questions.explanation: The pattern of missingness may itself be predictive (e.g. income missing → unusual income → different behaviour). Adding a flag preserves this information for downstream models.

questions.text: In a recipes pipeline, prep() learns imputation parameters from the full dataset including the future test set.
questions.explanation: prep() is called on the training data only. Parameters (medians, kNN neighbours) are learned from training data and then applied to new data via bake(). This prevents data leakage.

questions.text: Why is median preferred over mean for imputing a right-skewed variable like income?
options: The median is always larger than the mean for skewed data
The median is the most common value
The median is robust to extreme values; the mean is pulled toward outliers
The mean cannot be computed for income data
questions.explanation: For right-skewed distributions, the mean is pulled upward by a few very large values. The median represents the middle of the distribution and is unaffected by extreme outliers.

questions.text: kNN imputation is more accurate than median imputation because it:
options: Uses the k most similar complete records to estimate the missing value in context
Removes all rows with missing values
Uses the global mean regardless of the record's other features
questions.explanation: kNN finds the k nearest complete records and averages their values. A young Bronze-tier policyholder's missing BMI is estimated from similar young Bronze-tier policyholders — much more accurate than the global median.
